The Constitution and separation of powers

The US Constitution (1787) splits power between three branches that check each other:

Branch Who How they get there
Legislative Congress: Senate (100) + House of Representatives (435) Elected: senators for 6 years, representatives for 2
Executive President Elected every 4 years, at most two terms
Judicial Supreme Court (9 justices) Nominated by the president, confirmed by the Senate, serve for life
